title: Arctic Sea Ice Is Shrinking and Getting Thinner
summary:
The Arctic Ocean is covered by frozen seawater called sea ice. The ice grows in winter and shrinks in summer. Satellites have watched it since late 1978.

In 2026, the ice reached its smallest size on September 12. It covered about 4.6 million square kilometers. NASA and the National Snow and Ice Data Center say that tied for the 10th-lowest level on record. In March 2026, the winter ice tied March 2025 for the lowest winter peak ever recorded.

Over the past ten years, summer ice has stayed about the same instead of dropping fast. NASA researchers say more clouds blocked some sunlight. But the ice is still far below normal.

The ice is also getting younger and thinner, so it melts more easily. Scientists say rising temperatures are part of the cause. They think the Arctic could be nearly ice-free in summer at least once before 2050.
why_it_matters: Changes in Arctic ice affect polar animals and Earth's climate, which matters to everyone.
